lessons.title: Preparing for dispatch
lessons.html:
Preparing for dispatch

Dispatch is the last step before seed leaves the company. A mistake here reaches the customer directly: the wrong cultivar, wrong quantity, damaged bags or seed that is not approved for sale. Before planting season, a seed warehouse may load dozens of trucks a day for co-ops, dealers and large farmers, so good preparation is essential.

Check the order

  • Read the dispatch order or picking list: customer, delivery address, cultivar, treatment, pack size, quantity and lot numbers if specified.
  • Check that the order is approved, for example credit approval from the finance department.
  • Check that each lot is released for sale: laboratory results passed and the lot is out of quarantine. Never dispatch seed on hold.
  • Check the lot's test date. Seed regulations and company rules limit how long a test result is valid before retesting is needed.

Prepare the stock

  1. Pick the stock from the warehouse using first expiry, first out or first in, first out.
  2. Check every bag: correct label, lot number, cultivar, seal intact and no tears or wet spots.
  3. Count bags and check pallet quantities against the order.
  4. Keep picked stock in a marked dispatch bay, separate from other orders.

    5. Prepare the vehicle

    • Check that the truck or trailer is clean, dry and free of fertiliser, chemicals, feed or food. Treated seed must not be loaded with food or animal feed.
    • Check that the load can be covered with a sound tarpaulin to protect from rain and sun.
    • Check the vehicle and driver details on the order.

    Safety

    Forklifts cause serious injuries in warehouses. Only licensed and trained operators may drive them. Keep pedestrians out of loading areas, check stacked pallets are stable, and never stand under a raised load.

lessons.title: Dispatching the consignment
lessons.html:
Dispatching the consignment

Loading must protect the seed and the people doing the work, and the paperwork must match exactly what goes onto the truck.

Loading

  • Load according to the delivery route: the first drop goes in last, so it can be offloaded first.
  • Stack bags or pallets evenly so the load is stable and does not shift on gravel roads.
  • Do not throw or drop bags. Rough handling cracks seed and lowers germination.
  • Keep different cultivars and customers clearly separated in the load.
  • Cover the load fully and tie it down securely.

Manual handling

Seed bags are heavy. Lift with your knees bent and back straight, keep the bag close to your body and get help or use equipment for heavy loads. Report back pain early.

Documents

DocumentPurpose
Delivery note or invoiceShows what is delivered; customer signs on receipt
Lot numbers listTraceability if there is a complaint
Certificates (where required)Proof of quality or certification
Safety information for treated seedSafe handling by the customer
Export documents (if exporting)Phytosanitary and customs requirements

Final check before the truck leaves

  1. A second person checks the load against the delivery note: cultivar, quantity and lot numbers.
  2. The driver checks the load and signs for it.
  3. Record vehicle registration, driver name and time of departure.

If anything does not match, stop and correct it before the truck leaves. Fixing a mistake at the gate costs a few minutes; fixing it at a farm 400 km away costs much more.

lessons.title: Completing the dispatch process
lessons.html:
Completing the dispatch process

After the truck leaves, the dispatch is not finished until stock records, paperwork and follow-up are complete.

Updating stock records

  • Update the stock system immediately: deduct the dispatched quantity per lot.
  • Check that physical stock in the warehouse matches the system after the dispatch.
  • Report any difference to the supervisor straight away. Stock losses must be investigated.

Filing

  • File copies of the delivery note, the signed loading check and any certificates with the order.
  • When the signed proof of delivery comes back from the customer, attach it to the order.
  • Keep records for the period required by company procedure. Lot traceability records may be needed long after the seed is planted.

Returns and complaints

If a customer reports damaged bags, short delivery or wrong cultivar:

  1. Record the complaint with the order number and lot numbers.
  2. Check dispatch records to find what was loaded.
  3. Report to the supervisor or sales team to arrange collection, replacement or credit.
  4. Returned seed goes into quarantine until it has been checked. It must not go back into saleable stock without approval.

Housekeeping

Clean the dispatch bay, sweep up spilt seed (treated seed is swept up and disposed of as hazardous waste) and park forklifts in their bay with forks lowered. Return unused labels and seals to secure storage.

Learning from mistakes

Review errors such as wrong picks with the team. Often a small change, like clearer bay markings or a second check, stops the same mistake happening again.

Key points

  • Dispatch only approved, released lots that match the order.
  • Use a clean, dry vehicle; never load treated seed with food or feed.
  • Load carefully, cover the load and keep cultivars separated.
  • Paperwork must match the load exactly, checked by a second person.
  • Update stock records and keep traceability documents.
